text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm starting a PR for alerting rules tied to the new runtime telemetry dashboards (kv-cache hitrate, request_batch_latency_p95, model_queue_length). Need quick cross-team alignment on thresholds, SLO burn-rate windows, and oncall routing before I land.

samir: Thanks. Can you list the exact metrics and what they represent? helps me map to SLOs.

maya: Sure — short list:
- runtime_kv_cache_hitrate (ratio 0..1) — low values => more work to recompute prefixes
- request_batch_latency_seconds{quantile=\"0.95\"} — p95 latency for batched inference
- model_queue_length — instantaneous queued requests per model pool

ana: For burn-rate, recommend 5m and 1h windows. 5m for immediate pager, 1h for escalation if sustained. Example: >3x expected error/burn in 5m -> page infra; sustained 1h -> page platform + escalation.

jon: Agree on dual-window. Also want per-customer noisy-signal suppression — add a per-tenant dimension so we don't page on a single noisy consumer unless it crosses a hard absolute threshold.

samir: Threshold proposals:
- KV hitrate: page if < 0.65 for 5m, warning if < 0.75
- Batch p95: page if > 1.2s for 5m, escalate if > 1.2s for 1h
- Queue length: page if > 200 reqs/model-pool for 5m, warning at 120

ana: +1, but for queue_length also consider rate of growth (derivative) — if queue is growing fast we should page earlier even if raw <200. Suggest page if d/dt > 50 reqs/min sustained 3 consecutive 1m buckets.

maya: Good call about derivative. Can someone draft Prometheus-style alert snippets? I'll use them in the PR and wire them to PagerDuty.

ana: Drafting now:
```yaml
- alert: KVCacheLowHitrate
  expr: (sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))) > 0.35
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: \"KV cache hitrate low ({{ $value }})\"
    runbook: \"https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-low-hitrate\"

- alert: BatchLatencyHighP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_batch_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_pool)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: \"Batch p95 > 1.2s for model_pool={{ $labels.model_pool }}\"
    runbook: \"https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batch-latency\"

- alert: ModelQueueGrowingFast
  expr: increase(model_queue_length[3m]) > 150
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: \"Model queue growing quickly (model_pool={{ $labels.model_pool }})\"
    runbook: \"https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-backpressure\"
```

jon: That looks solid. For Page routing, map severity=page -> pagerduty service: infra-runtime-prod; for severity=warning -> platform-notify (Slack + email). We should avoid paging platform for cache blips under 10min unless noisy.

samir: On SLO burn: define SLOs (examples):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% for hosted inference control-plane (use request errors and timeouts)
- Latency SLO: 95% requests < 800ms (scaled by model class)
Tie alerts to burn-rate: alert when burn_rate_5m > 4x and projected 24h burn would exceed budget.

maya: How do we compute burn_rate in alerts? do we store the error budget metric or compute on the fly?

ana: compute on the fly with recording rules, then use rate() on the error_budget_burn_total. Example recording: error_budget_burn_5m = (errors_in_5m / total_requests_5m) / SLO_target.

samir: We'll need a small docs blurb in the PR describing the mapping from these alerts to PagerDuty escalation policies. Suggest primary -> infra-oncall, second -> platform-oncall, third -> engineering-esc (if no ack in 15m). Also include a read-only dashboard widget for the team oncall view.

maya: Who owns the PagerDuty service creation and oncall mapping? I can create the alert rules but not the PD objects.

jon: I can create the PagerDuty services and connect the alertmanager webhook. Assign to me for PD setup.

ana: I'll own the Prometheus alert PR and add the recording rules for burn rate. I'll also add the per-tenant label to suppress noisy single-tenant pages (notification class = noisy -> don't page unless abs threshold crossed).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Created branch alerting/kv-batch-queue in infra/prometheus-config. CI run queued.

maya: Great. Action items summary:
- ana: PR with recording rules + alerts, include runbooks and tenant-suppression logic — due Wed EOD
- jon: create PagerDuty services, escalation policies, and confirm webhook — due Wed EOD
- samir: own SLO definitions doc and mapping to alerts (burn-rate math) — due Tue noon
- maya: wire dashboard panels to show alert state and add per-oncall view + add ops runbook links — due Thu

oncall-bot: reminder: infra-oncall rotation is @diane this week, platform-oncall is @sam

samir: I can be platform-oncall backup during the initial rollout window.

maya: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready and request reviews from @ana @jon @samir. If anyone sees gaps in thresholds or escalation logic, flag in the PR comments so we can iterate before enabling paging in prod.

jon: One more ask — add a temporary mute window for non-prod clusters when we flip the alerts on, so we don't wake people for pre-prod noise.

maya: Noted, will add a label filter cluster=prod to the alert rules by default and a separate non-prod rule for burn testing. I'll also add a checklist item to the PR to toggle non-prod when ready.

maya: OK landing this thread — will update thread_ts with PR and PD service IDs once done. :thumbsup:
